Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The pitch is being rolled on the pitch and now we see the two openers for England, Ben Duckett and Dan Lawrence make their way out to the middle. The Sri Lankan players are already in their respective positions. Asitha Fernando to start proceedings with the ball.
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Not much to talk about the batting performance of Sri Lanka! Kamindu Mendis was the only shining light for them with another classy knock. He made 74 off 120 balls but just kept losing partners towards the end, and the top order have been ineffective in this series which is a big concern for them. They find themselves in a really difficult position here and if England comes out to bat, their bowlers will need to be on point to restrict them to as low as possible, or else they could be chasing something massive here. The only positive for them is that, even though they have not defeated England in a Test for over a decade, they have also not lost to England at Lord's for over a decade as well. Seems like the wait for one team will definitely come to an end here. Join us in a bit for England's second innings and expect some fireworks.

Sri Lanka have been wrapped up for 196 here! England have the option to force a follow-on here, but it does not look like they are going to as their openers briskly make their way to the dressing room. It was a brilliant all-round bowling effort from the hosts. Chris Woakes and Olly Stone set the tone for them, and then the other two pacers, Gus Atkinson and Matthew Potts picked up the pace and all four of them shared 8 wickets equally while Shoaib Bashir chipped in with one. Ollie Pope also enforced an excellent run out to break the partnership between Kamindu Mendis and Lahiru Kumara which helped them to bowl them out quickly and they still have a big lead of 231 runs.

OUT! CAUGHT! Gus Atkinson gets the job done for England! Gus Atkinson once again fires a bumper outside off and once again Kamindu Mendis looks to slap it down the ground but miscues the shot. The ball hits the top of the of willow and loops towards mid off . Chris Woakes makes no mistake and takes a comfortable catch. Sri Lanka posted 196 on the board and trailed by 231 runs!

After the event of back-to-back wickets, the trail of wickets started to fall for Sri Lanka. The English pacers were disciplined enough to maintain their lines and lengths and capitalized the situation perfectly. England still have their lone spinner, Shoaib Bashir, who is still fresh and hasn't bowled a single spell in this inning. However, the young Lankan prospect, Kamindu Mendis is still on the pitch, and the English bowling would love to push a bit more to take this one down cause they have already witnessed his master-class strokeplay in the first Test match. Sri Lanka though still trails by 298 with only three wickets left and needs something special to reduce that margin. Another thrilling session of play is undoubtedly on the horizon. Stick around as the action resumes at 3.00 pm GMT!

TEA, DAY 2 - Session Summary - Things are going from bad to worse for Sri Lanka. Just after the Lunch break, Olly Stone didn't have to drop a sweat to get another breakthrough in the very same over where he got his first just before the Lunch. After the fall of the wicket, Angelo Mathews and Dinesh Chandimal brought the composure back on the crease and were coordinating well. But as soon as they were two runs close to completing their 50-run-mark partnership, Matthew Potts joined the attack and hunted down the dangerous-looking Mathews with a ripper. Potts in the same over removed the Lankan skipper for a duck.

Sri Lanka on the other hand, needs a partnership, the wicket is good, the second day is probably the best one to bat and they would love to make good use of it. They did lose one early but Karunaratne and Nissanka managed to get through a few tough overs. Can they start a fight back after the break? A testing second session coming up for them.

They managed to take their score to over 400 and that was all thanks to Atkinson who got up a fine ton and then dismissed an opener too in the little overs they had to bowl before the break.
